title: PlayStation 5
description: Home video game console by Sony
wiki_lead:
The PlayStation 5 (PS5) is a home video game console developed by Sony Interactive Entertainment as the fifth iteration of their PlayStation brand. It was announced as the successor to the PlayStation 4 in April 2019, and was launched in Australia, Japan, New Zealand, North America, and South Korea on November 12, 2020, and worldwide a week later. The PS5 is part of the ninth generation of video game consoles, along with Microsoft's Xbox Series X/S consoles, which were released the same month.
The base model includes an optical disc drive compatible with Ultra HD Blu-ray discs. The Digital Edition lacks this drive, as a lower-cost model for buying games only through download. The two variants were launched simultaneously. Slimmer hardware revisions of both models replaced the original models on sale in November 2023. A PlayStation 5 Pro model was released on November 7, 2024, featuring a faster GPU, improved ray tracing, and introducing an AI-driven upscaling technology. 
The PlayStation 5's main hardware features include a solid-state drive customized for high-speed data streaming to enable significant improvements in storage performance, a GPU by AMD capable of 4K resolution display at up to 120 frames per second, hardware-accelerated ray tracing for realistic lighting and reflections, and the Tempest Engine for hardware-accelerated 3D audio effects. Other features include the DualSense controller with haptic feedback, backward compatibility with the majority of PlayStation 4 and PlayStation VR games, and the PlayStation VR2 headset.

History


Development

The lead architect of the PlayStation console line, Mark Cerny, implemented a two-year feedback cycle after the launch of the PlayStation 4. This entailed regularly visiting Sony's first-party developers at two-year intervals to find out what concerns they had about Sony's hardware and how it could be improved in console refreshes or for the next generation. This feedback directly influenced the priorities of the development team. During the development of the PlayStation 5, a central challenge revolved around addressing the length of loading times for games. Cerny said several developers, including Epic Games' Tim Sweeney, told him that standard I/O speed of a hard disk drive was now a limiting factor in pushing game development. Slow data rates placed limits on the size of data being loaded into the game, the physical location of data on the storage medium, and the duplication of data across the medium in order to reduce load times. An important goal was to find ways to reduce loading time, particularly in games that stream or dynamically load new game areas as the player moves through the game world.

grok_lead: The PlayStation 5 (PS5) is a ninth-generation home video game console developed and marketed by Sony Interactive Entertainment as the successor to the PlayStation 4. It was first revealed in a technical presentation on March 18, 2020, and launched on November 12, 2020, in select regions including North America, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, and South Korea, followed by a worldwide release on November 19, 2020. The console features hardware including a custom AMD Ryzen Zen 2 CPU with 8 cores and 16 threads running at up to 3.5 GHz, a custom AMD Radeon RDNA 2 GPU delivering up to 10.28 teraflops with hardware-accelerated ray tracing, 16 GB of GDDR6 memory with 448 GB/s bandwidth, and an 825 GB custom SSD providing 5.5 GB/s raw I/O throughput (expandable to 8-9 GB/s with compression). Key features of the PS5 include reduced load times enabled by its custom SSD with raw I/O throughput of 5.5 GB/s (expandable to 8â9 GB/s with compression), support for 4K resolution at up to 120 Hz, 8K output, variable refresh rate (VRR), and HDR via HDMI 2.1; Tempest 3D AudioTech for spatial sound; and the DualSense wireless controller, which incorporates haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, a built-in microphone, and a touchpad. The console supports an Ultra HD Blu-ray optical drive in its standard model for physical media playback, while the PS5 Digital Edition variant omits the drive for a lower price point; both models are backwards compatible with the vast majority of PlayStation 4 games. In November 2023, Sony released the PS5 Slim, a compact redesign with a slimmer form factor, an included horizontal stand, 1 TB SSD storage, and the option to add a detachable disc drive to the Digital Edition (CFI-2000 series). On November 7, 2024, Sony released the PS5 Pro, an enhanced mid-generation refresh with a more powerful GPU offering 16.7 teraflops (versus 10.28 teraflops on the PS5 Slim), 2â3Ã faster ray tracing, AI-driven upscaling via PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)âupgraded in February 2026 to a new version providing enhanced image quality, with a March 2026 system software update introducing an "Enhance PSSR Image Quality" toggle that enables instant graphics improvements for existing PSSR-supported games without requiring patches, starting with new titles like Resident Evil Requiem (launched February 27, 2026). A minor unannounced hardware revision (CFI-7100 series) with improved power efficiency shipped in late 2025; otherwise no new models or performance hardware updates for the PS5 Pro were released or announced in 2025 or 2026, and the PSSR enhancements were software-based, with a major update to the PSSR upscaler announced by Mark Cerny on February 27, 2026. The console has 2 TB SSD storage, and Wi-Fi 7 support, with graphics performance roughly matched or exceeded by mid-range 2025 PC GPUs such as the Nvidia RTX 5060 Ti (16GB) and AMD RX 9060 XT (16GB) in many cross-platform titles according to Digital Foundry benchmarks, which show PCs often delivering higher frame rates especially with advanced upscaling (DLSS/FSR), though the PS5 Pro can have an edge in specific optimized ray tracing scenarios. In November 2025, Sony's CFO stated that the PS5 is only in the middle of its lifecycle and that the company is planning to expand support even further, with interpretations suggesting potential extension up to around 2030 (approximately 10 years from launch). As a variant of the PS5, the PS5 Pro will continue to receive new games, including Pro-enhanced titles, as long as the PS5 generation is supported, with many new titles announced for release in 2026 and likely beyond; no exact end date for new game releases has been announced. On March 27, 2026, the official PlayStation Blog announced price increases for the PS5, PS5 Digital Edition, PS5 Pro, and PlayStation Portal due to "continued pressures in the global economic landscape." The changes take effect April 2, 2026, in regions including the U.S., U.K., Europe, and Japan. New U.S. prices: PS5 (disc) $649.99, PS5 Digital $599.99, PS5 Pro $899.99, PlayStation Portal $249.99. As of June 30, 2026, the PS5 has shipped 95.3 million units worldwide, surpassing the PlayStation 3's lifetime shipments of 87.4 million, making it Sony's most profitable console generation to date and generating over $136 billion in total revenue across hardware, software, and services as of 2025. In January 2026, Circana reported that the PlayStation 5 led the US gaming hardware market in both unit and dollar sales, ahead of the newly launched Nintendo Switch 2 in second place, despite a 17% year-over-year decline in PS5 sales; overall US hardware spending rose 16% to $248 million, partly due to Switch 2 sales. The console's ecosystem includes access to the PlayStation Store for digital downloads, PlayStation Network for online multiplayer and cross-play (generally not restricted by account region, allowing play with players using different region PSN accounts while digital purchases, DLC, and subscriptions remain region-specific to the account's country), and exclusive titles from first-party studios like Naughty Dog and Santa Monica Studio, alongside support for PlayStation VR2 virtual reality headset. As of September 2025, the PS5 held the largest share of the ninth-generation home console market, outselling the Xbox Series X/S by an estimated ratio of approximately 2.5:1 according to available industry data, with PS5 shipments at 84.2 million units compared to roughly 33-34 million for the Xbox Series X/S.
